title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions

meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on inverse trigonometric functions for Texas TEKS P.2F and P.2H: exact values, domain and range of arcsin and arccos, compositions and angle problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: arcsin gives an angle in [−π/2, π/2]; arccos in [0, π].
key_sub: The input of arcsin and arccos must be from −1 to 1.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • sin−1 x (arcsin) gives the angle in [−π/2, π/2] whose sine is x. Its domain is −1 ≤ x ≤ 1.
  • cos−1 x (arccos) gives the angle in [0, π]. tan−1 x gives the angle in (−π/2, π/2) for any x.
  • These ranges are why the domain of sine and cosine is restricted: so each output comes from only one angle.
  • For tan(sin−1 a), draw a right triangle with the given ratio.

Examples

Example

cos−1(−12)

The range is [0, π]

cos(2π/3) = −1/2

Answer: 2π3

items.q: Aaliyah flies a kite on 120 m of string. The kite is 40 m above her hand. To the nearest degree, what angle does the string make with the horizontal?
items.e: The height is opposite and the string is the hypotenuse: θ = sin⁻¹(40/120) ≈ 19°.

items.q: A road sign says the grade is 5%: the road rises 5 ft for every 100 ft horizontally. To the nearest tenth of a degree, what angle does the road make with the horizontal?
items.e: θ = tan⁻¹(5/100) ≈ 2.9°. A 5% grade is not 5°.
